facts.situation: James and Caroline Whitmore are joint clients with an agreed risk profile of 4, balanced to moderate. James completed the sale of his business in April; the transition has been busy and somewhat emotional for both. A completion payment of £850,000 has been received and is held in a solicitor's client account, with £200,000 already committed to repaying a bridging loan due shortly. A deferred earnout of up to £400,000 may be paid over the next two years, contingent on business revenue targets; none has been received and it is not guaranteed. They seek long-term growth and a tax-efficient investment base to replace James's income when he steps back from full-time work in about three years. They currently need no portfolio income. Possible consultancy work is unsettled. Future help with grandchildren's school fees and a possible charitable donation are aspirations only, with no action intended in this report. James is concerned about pension over-contributions.

actions.action: Repay the bridging loan from the business-sale completion proceeds.
Top up James's Holloway ISA, H4-ISA-J, using his allowance for the new tax year.
Top up Caroline's Holloway ISA, H4-ISA-C, using her allowance for the new tax year.
Contribute to James's Brightwell SIPP, B4-SIPP-J, at an appropriate level within applicable limits.
Contribute to Caroline's Brightwell SIPP, B4-SIPP-C, at an appropriate level within applicable limits.
Add completion proceeds to the Holloway joint GIA, H4-GIA-HJ.
Partially disinvest and rebalance the Holloway joint GIA, H4-GIA-HJ.
Place the remaining completion proceeds into a new jointly held investment account.
Leave the Meridian offshore bond, M4-BOND-J, unchanged for now and revisit at the next review.
